Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):  2-month history of escalating anxiety related to new stressful job; insomnia (sleep 3–4 h/night); episodic palpitations; low energy and anhedonia. No chronic physical diseases recorded.  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):  Mother has history of depression. No other conditions recorded.  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  None reported.  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):  Not recorded.  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:  Not recorded.  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:  
  • Physical activity previously included running/tennis; markedly reduced due to anxiety/fatigue.  
  • Diet unchanged except increased chocolate intake when feeling low.  
  • Tobacco: occasional smoker.  
  • Alcohol: binge drinking on Friday/Saturday (likely exceeds recommended limits) plus occasional weekday wine with parents.  
  • No recreational drug use.  
- Hearing and vision concerns:  Not recorded.  
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm):  
  • Persistent worry about work, dread leaving house, palpitations.  
  • Low mood and loss of enjoyment; no suicidal ideation or self-harm thoughts.  
  • No prior similar episodes; no counselling to date.  
- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors:  
  • Lives with parents; good family support.  
  • Workplace stress due to hostile supervisor.

- Vital signs: BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  Not recorded (telehealth).

- Blood tests: fasting glucose and lipids preferred; HbA1c if diabetes present/suspected:  Planned “basic blood tests” (specific panels not detailed).  
- Renal function and liver function tests if clinically indicated:  Planned but not specified.  
- ECG if cardiac risk factors present or baseline:  Not recorded.  
- Cervical screening if eligible and due:  Not recorded.  
- Mammography if eligible and not up to date:  Not recorded.  
- Faecal occult blood test if due:  Not recorded.  
- Bone density (DEXA) if osteoporosis risk present:  Not recorded.  

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: New-onset anxiety temporally related to starting stressful job; significant functional impact (sleep disruption, social withdrawal, reduced enjoyment, palpitations). No suicidal ideation. Physical causes not yet excluded.

Working diagnosis: Adjustment disorder with anxiety (early generalized anxiety disorder). Supported by transcript evidence of psychosocial stressor and DDx high-likelihood ranking.

Considerations:  
• Major depressive disorder with anxious distress (medium likelihood—low mood, anhedonia, fatigue).  
• Hyperthyroidism or other medical causes of palpitations (low–medium likelihood; to be screened via planned blood work).  

Management:  
• Provided information and link for NHS self-referral talking therapy (CBT).  
• Advised online anxiety/sleep resources.  
• Ordered basic blood tests to exclude physiological triggers of palpitations/anxiety; arrange GP follow-up 1 week post-results.  
• Discussed possible pharmacotherapy if symptoms worsen or non-pharmacological measures ineffective.  

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  Discuss sleep hygiene; advised moderating alcohol; encouraged gradual return to exercise once anxiety controlled.  
- Patient health goals and priorities:  Reduce daily anxiety, improve sleep, maintain work attendance.  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA):  Not recorded.  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports):  
  • Self-referral to NHS talking therapy (CBT).  
  • Advised contacting GP sooner if deterioration.  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled:  GP review after blood test results (~1 week).  

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral:  Planned (talking therapy).  
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management:  Not indicated currently.  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified:  Not recorded.  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening:  Not recorded.  
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected:  Not recorded.  
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health:  Not recorded.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
1. Adjustment disorder with anxiety / early Generalized Anxiety Disorder – High likelihood: clear onset after job change, pervasive worry, somatic anxiety symptoms.  
2. Major depressive disorder (anxious distress specifier) – Medium likelihood: low mood, anhedonia, fatigue, family history; no suicidality.  
3. Hyperthyroidism (e.g., Graves’) – Low–Medium likelihood: palpitations and insomnia could be thyrotoxic; to be ruled out with blood tests.

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: No vitals, anthropometrics, or cardiovascular/thyroid blood panels documented; immunisation status, cervical screening, alcohol units/week not quantified.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality notes: Audio appears complete; no physical exam possible due to telehealth; patient age (29 y) does not meet “55 y+ Indigenous Health Assessment” criteria—template applied as instructed.
